questions.prompt: On a distance–time graph, what does a horizontal (flat) section mean?
questions.explain: Distance stays the same as time passes.

questions.prompt: On a distance–time graph, a steeper line means…
questions.explain: More distance in the same time.

questions.prompt: A water tank graph rises, stays flat, then falls to zero. What happened?
options: The tank filled, stayed full for a while, then drained
questions.explain: Rise = filling, flat = no change, fall = draining.

questions.prompt: A graph of tea temperature drops steeply at first, then levels off. Why?
options: Tea cools quickly when very hot, then more slowly near room temperature
Tea cools at a steady rate
questions.explain: The bigger the difference from room temperature, the faster it cools.

questions.prompt: In the bath graph, the water depth suddenly jumps up without the tap running. What is the best explanation?
questions.explain: A body displaces water, so the level jumps.

questions.prompt: Describe a journey that would give this distance–time graph: a straight line rising for 10 minutes, flat for 5 minutes, then a straight line back down to 0 over 20 minutes.
questions.modelAnswer: I walk away from home at a steady speed for 10 minutes, stop somewhere (e.g. a shop) for 5 minutes, then walk back home at a slower steady speed, taking 20 minutes, because the return line is less steep.
questions.explain: Criterion C: interpret a graph in words.

questions.prompt: A ball is thrown up. Its height–time graph curves up, flattens at the top, then curves down. What happens at the flat top?
options: The ball is momentarily still before falling
The ball has hit the ground
questions.explain: At the top, its vertical speed is zero for an instant.

questions.prompt: Adam walks 1000 m to school. On his graph he covers the first 400 m in 5 minutes. What is his speed in metres per minute for that part?
